To perfectly capture the fiercely fastidious, highly organized nature of a ruthless mob enforcer, Charlie Hunnam and director Guy Ritchie decided to completely overhaul the character’s wardrobe. Instead of dressing him like a traditional, heavily bruised street thug, Ritchie personally took Hunnam to an incredibly high-end London tailor, meticulously crafting an impeccably sharp, profoundly expensive array of bespoke suits and knitwear. By intentionally dressing a violently dangerous hitman like an extraordinarily refined gentleman who absolutely despises a mess, Ritchie masterfully proves that the most terrifying cinematic enforcers don’t always wear leather jackets—sometimes they wear perfectly pressed cardigans.
⠀
The Gentlemen (2019), directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant. A brilliantly calculating, highly successful American weed kingpin in London attempts to massively cash out his sprawling, fiercely lucrative criminal empire, accidentally triggering a wildly chaotic, deeply explosive underworld war filled with blackmail, bribery, and heavily armed double-crosses.
